charter-and-supplemental-charter-of-the-: This volume prints the founding legal documents of the Hudson's Bay Company — the 1670 royal charter from Charles II granting it vast trading rights over northern North America. These few pages of legal language shaped the history of Canada, opening the fur trade that drew Europeans deep into the continent. Essential reading for understanding how Canada began.
the-curlytops-at-uncle-frank-s-ranch-or-: Howard Garis — creator of Uncle Wiggily — sends the Curlytops to Uncle Frank's ranch for ponyback adventures. The cheerful twins find fun, mild scrapes, and new friends among cowboys and cattle. Wholesome, old-fashioned children's entertainment from a master of the genre.
my-four-years-in-germany: Ambassador James Gerard tells of his four years in Germany — from peace through the Great War's outbreak. His inside account of the Kaiser's court was a wartime sensation. History from the diplomatic front line. From the Kaiser's dinners to wartime Berlin, his narrative never loses its grip.
richard-of-jamestown-a-story-of-the-virg: James Otis — the beloved author of Toby Tyler — tells the story of Richard of Jamestown and the Virginia colony's hard founding years. Hunger, Indians, and Captain John Smith fill this stirring tale for boys. American history made thrilling for young readers, who will cheer Richard's courage.
through-five-republics-on-horseback-bein: George Whitfield Ray rode on horseback through five South American republics, and this is the account of his many wanderings. Part missionary, part explorer, he crossed mountains and jungles few travelers had seen. His narrative blends high adventure with deep Christian faith. Strange peoples, wild lands, and constant peril fill the pages. A remarkable record of travel in a little-known continent.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-flav: This reference piece covers Flavigny, the Burgundian abbey famed for its anise sweets. Monks have made the little candies for centuries. Henri Leclercq gives its history. A sweet-toothed corner of old France. The anise drops are still made by the old recipe today.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-pont: A 1913 article on Pontigny, the Burgundian house that sheltered Becket. Exiled saints found refuge in its cloister. Edmond Obrecht tells its proud tale. Sanctuary for the persecuted. Langton hid there from King John's wrath. Its church is the purest Cistercian building in France.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-savi: The Encyclopedia on Savigny, mother of a whole order. Its grey monks joined Cîteaux in time. Edmond Obrecht traces its brief glory. A reform that merged into a greater one. Its white habit passed into Cistercian use. Its daughters dotted Normandy and England.
